held.reason: LSI mānus “Man” resembles an Indo-Aryan mānuṣa-type word, but the immediate donor and exact source form are not established; DEDR 399 Kodagu a·ḷï/ a·ṇï is a different stem.
LSI payyu “Cow” occurs incidentally in DEDR 2659 cuḷḷi payyu “spotted cow”, but that article etymologizes “spot”; it does not establish the ancestry or immediate donor of payyu.
DEDR 2165 gives Kodagu kori “sheep” and Tulu kuri “sheep”; LSI kuri is “He goat”. Form and animal sense are close but not exact, and the possible borrowed/immediate donor path is unresolved.
LSI kuttaḍ “Bad boy” is a nominal phrase/derived form; no matching Kodagu DEDR stem or safe component analysis was established.
LSI kullona “Sit” has no secure match in the Kodagu DEDR sit/descend entries; DEDR 502 explicitly questions a different aḷa- “sit down” comparison.
LSI ēḍa “My” may be a reduced first-person possessive, but its vowel and absence of n do not match the Kodagu en-/nan-/na·- obliques quoted in DEDR 5160 closely enough for a confident assignment.
LSI entuna “Stand” differs from DEDR 3675 Kodagu nill- “stand”; no matching en-/entu- stem or derivation has been established.
LSI pār “Run” has no secure Kodagu DEDR match; DEDR 1041 Kodagu o·ḍ- “run” is a different stem and DEDR 3949 para- is “crawl/spread”.
LSI orama “Hair” has no securely matched Kodagu DEDR head or immediate donor; DEDR 3103 talami “hair” and DEDR 2655 jïṭṭï “tuft” are different stems.
LSI payyu “Cow” is a separate survey record from the male/elicitation section. The incidental DEDR 2659 phrase cuḷḷi payyu does not etymologize payyu itself.
LSI pakki “Bird” appears incidentally in DEDR 1608 and 5370 compound bird names, but neither article etymologizes the simplex or proves an immediate borrowing donor.

LSI ākuḷu ittery “They were” has two words, but DEDR 1 lists ākuḷu under Tulu rather than Kodagu and DEDR 480 does not quote Kodagu itter-. The survey response may cross lect or paradigm boundaries, so neither ordered component is assigned yet.

LSI eŋga poyipa nōpuva “We beat” is a three-word response with unexplained nōpuva. DEDR 5154 eŋga and DEDR 4534 poyy can be recognized, but the third token needs source review before assigning a complete ordered analysis.
LSI yeŋla honeo “We go” lacks the ordinary Kodagu eŋga and po·- stems in DEDR 5154 and 4572. Both words need separate verification; a familiar gloss is insufficient to normalize them.
LSI ayanḍa “Their” may use a distal a-/ay- oblique, but DEDR 1 quotes neither this Kodagu stem nor this possessive ending. The relation to avaŋg/avu remains tentative.
